cita: Xie et al. (2026). PASK: Toward Intent-Aware Proactive Agents with Long-Term Memory.
problema: Current AI systems are purely reactive ('you ask, I answer'), which breaks down under real-world timing/context constraints (can't query mid-meeting or mid-video, awkward to invoke) and lacks any evolving memory of the user, preventing proactive, personalized, long-term assistance rather than isolated query responses.
mecanismo: The DD-MM-PAS paradigm: IntentFlow (a Demand-Detector + MemLoader dual-model) predicts a per-step control token (silent / fast_intervention / full_assistance) from streaming input; a hybrid three-tier memory backs the full_assistance path -- Workspace Memory (session context window, organized by a dedicated memory agent), User Memory (cache-like stable-trait profile with KV-cache reuse for near-zero added latency), and Global Memory (an asynchronous LLM-RAG store over long-term interaction history); post-session (offline, zero online-latency-impact) memory evolution applies a time-decayed Bayesian update to reconcile conflicts and forgetting in user traits and to compress/prune Global Memory.
evaluacion: LatentNeeds-Bench (real-world, user-consented data refined through thousands of rounds of human editing) measures turn-level balanced demand-detection accuracy against multiple proprietary/open frontier LLM baselines in single-turn and multi-turn/long-conversation settings, plus per-turn latency measurements and a qualitative user study (quiz scores after a 5-minute video, with/without Pask).
numeros_clave: IntentFlow reaches 83.1 overall Demand-split accuracy, matching Gemini-3-Flash (83.3) and beating GPT-5-Nano (71.2)/GPT-5-Mini (66.5) (Table1); in multi-turn settings IntentFlow maintains >80% balanced accuracy across all turn buckets while the strongest baseline degrades from 56.2 to 48.7 (Fig.8); user study: quiz score after a 5-min video improves from ~6 (no Pask) to ~6-7.5 (with Pask), a +1 to +1.5 point gain (Sec6.5.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Workspace Memory (Sec4.1) keeps the full within-session interaction/task state, continuously organized by a dedicated memory agent, functioning as an explicit ongoing-task-state store MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could adopt as a first-class memory tier.

Multi-turn balanced-accuracy measurement (Table3/Fig.8) shows IntentFlow's memory-grounded full_assistance mode sustaining >80% accuracy while a strong baseline degrades, empirically supporting MF's measured-retrieval stance.

Post-session, strictly offline conflict-resolution and compression (Sec4.3, zero online-latency impact) is a concrete pattern for scheduling heavy memory maintenance outside the hot path, which MF could mirror for its own consolidation cadence.
The time-decayed Bayesian trait update that reinforces matched evidence and explicitly resolves conflicting user traits (Sec4.3, ResolveConflict) is a concrete staleness/conflict-handling mechanism.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main benchmark), Fig.8 (multi-turn degradation) and Sec6.5.3 (user study); an industry-lab preprint (Pask-Core/NTU/NUS) with a public demo -- the memory contribution itself is validated mostly qualitatively (Sec6.5.2/6.5.3), not via a controlled memory-specific ablation.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models.
problema: Retrieval-based external memory is cheap online but unstable in accuracy (noisy query construction/candidate filtering), while LLM-driven memory operations are more accurate but accumulate latency from repeated large-model calls over long interactions -- an efficiency/effectiveness trade-off with no system that resolves both.
mecanismo: Modularizes memory into STM (SLM context window)/MTM (per-user episodic summaries with embeddings)/LTM (de-identified, graph-structured consolidated knowledge), coordinated by three specialized small language models: a Controller (SLM-1) that rewrites queries into hypothetical-query retrieval plans with a fixed Top-K budget across MTM/LTM, a Selector (SLM-2) that runs two-stage retrieval (vector coarse-retrieval at 2K candidates, then semantic-consistency re-ranking down to K), and a Writer (SLM-3) that incrementally writes/merges MTM entries; heavier abstraction and LTM consolidation are deferred to an offline large-context LLM, strictly decoupled from the online path.
evaluacion: LoCoMo (5 question categories) and DialSim (1,300 multi-party TV-show sessions) across 6 backbones (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B) vs 4 baselines (ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT, A-MEM); component ablation (semantic reranking, HQ routing, MTM, offline consolidation, graph structure); P50/P95 retrieval and end-to-end latency measurement across all methods.
numeros_clave: Average F1 improvement of ~2.5 over A-MEM on LoCoMo (e.g. GPT-4o multi-hop F1 34.52 vs A-MEM 32.86, Table2); DialSim SBERT similarity 23.40 vs A-MEM's 19.51 (Table3); median retrieval latency 83ms and end-to-end 581ms vs A-MEM's 856ms/914ms (Table4); ablation on Llama-3.2-1B: full F1=4.12, w/o MTM drops to 3.75, w/o semantic reranking to 3.83 (Sec4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured P50 retrieval latency of 83ms and end-to-end 581ms, far below A-MEM's 856ms/914ms while beating it on F1 (Table2/4), directly confirms MF's premise that structural decoupling (online-lightweight vs offline-heavy), not brute-force LLM calls, is the real cost lever.

The STM/MTM/LTM split with a fixed Top-K budget and two-stage coarse-then-rerank retrieval (Sec3.3-3.4) is a concrete tiered-index pattern MF's TIER-INDICE could adopt to keep the online path bounded and cheap.
Offline confidence-decay on weakly-supported LTM candidates plus evidence-driven merge/update/drop decisions (Sec3.6) is a reusable staleness-management mechanism separate from the online write path.

notes: Numbers from Table2/3 (main LoCoMo/DialSim results), Table4 (latency) and Sec4.3 (ablation); solid controlled ablation and latency benchmarking across 6 backbones, one of the more rigorously evaluated papers in this batch.

cita: Halak (2026). NLM: Neural Long Memory — Hybrid Long-Term Memory for AI Agents.
problema: Standard RAG retrieves purely by semantic similarity, ignoring when a memory was created, how often it has been accessed, and how factually specific it is -- causing failures under temporal conflicts (stale vs current fact), frequency blindness (rarely vs frequently used facts treated equally), and importance blindness (vague vs specific facts scored as near-synonyms).
mecanismo: A composite retrieval score S(m,q) = 0.5*semantic + 0.2*exponential-time-decay (90-day half-life) + 0.2*normalized-access-frequency + 0.1*importance-heuristic (numbers/proper-nouns/length in CPU mode, or a zero-shot classifier on GPU); automatic consolidation merges a new memory into an existing near-duplicate (cosine distance < 0.15) rather than storing it separately; an associative-memory graph links memories above a similarity threshold for one-hop expansion at search time.
evaluacion: A small, self-constructed controlled benchmark of 100 memories (60 in 20 test triples + 40 background fillers) and 30 queries (10 each: temporal / frequency / importance categories), comparing NLM's top-1 retrieval accuracy against plain cosine-similarity RAG; no standard benchmark (e.g. LoCoMo) or external baseline system is used.
numeros_clave: Overall top-1 accuracy 87% (NLM) vs 50% (RAG), a +37 percentage-point gain; per-category: Temporal 70% vs 10% (+60pp), Frequency 100% vs 80% (+20pp), Importance 90% vs 60% (+30pp) (Sec4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The controlled 30-query benchmark directly measures that adding recency/frequency/importance signals beats pure cosine-similarity retrieval by 37pp overall (Sec4.2), a small but clean demonstration supporting MF's measured-retrieval stance.

The explicit temporal-conflict category (older vs newer near-identical fact, resolved via exponential recency decay, Sec4.3) is a minimal reusable staleness-resolution test case MF could reuse to validate its own anti-drift retrieval.

Near-duplicate merging by cosine-distance threshold with frequency-counter incrementing (Sec3.2) is a simple, low-cost consolidation rule, useful as a baseline pattern rather than a sophisticated mechanism.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- a single independent-researcher pip-package write-up (a marketing-style paper for 'neural-long-memory') validated only on a tiny, self-constructed benchmark (100 memories, 30 queries), not on any standard dataset like LoCoMo; the author explicitly acknowledges this scope limitation (Sec5.2).

cita: Feng et al. (2026). Thought-Retriever: Don't Just Retrieve Raw Data, Retrieve Thoughts for Memory-Augmented Agentic Systems.
problema: Retrieval-augmented LLMs are fundamentally constrained by context length: they can only pull top-K raw data chunks from external knowledge bases that may hold millions of chunks, so relevant evidence scattered across many chunks (low recall) or blurred by generic static summaries (hierarchical RALMs) cannot be faithfully surfaced.
mecanismo: After answering each query, the LLM's own answer is distilled into a validated 'thought' (query-conditioned, abstractive, confidence- and novelty-checked via a discrete confidence flag and a similarity-based redundancy check) and added to a growing thought memory; future queries retrieve from the union of raw chunks and accumulated thoughts by embedding similarity, so the memory self-evolves and balances low-level facts with high-level distilled reasoning without extra fine-tuning; a root-source mapping traces any thought back to its originating raw chunks for provenance/verification.
evaluacion: A new benchmark AcademicEval (built from real arXiv papers, Abstract-single/Abstract-multi/Related-multi tasks) plus two public datasets (GovReport, WCEP), against 12 baselines (BM25, TF-IDF, 4 dense retrievers, IRCoT, RECOMP, full-context truncation, 2 long-context LLMs) using F1 (ROUGE-L) and LLM-judged win rate; published in TMLR with public OpenReview.
numeros_clave: Average increase of at least 7.6% in F1 and 16% in win rate across all datasets/tasks vs the best baselines (Sec4.2); e.g. Abstract-single F1=0.290 (Thought-Retriever) vs best baseline Nous Hermes-32k 0.247, win rate 50% (tie-reference) vs baselines all below 30% (Table2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Thoughts are query-conditioned abstractions layered on top of raw chunks and retrieved alongside them (Sec2.1-2.3), a concrete derived-index-as-cache pattern that stays query-driven (not a static precompiled summary tree) -- relevant to MF's TIER-INDICE design.

The root-source mapping O-hat(.) that recursively traces any thought back to the raw chunks that grounded it (Sec2.1) is a formal provenance mechanism directly applicable to MF's staleness/poisoning concerns.

The confidence+novelty gated thought-memory update (only add a thought if confident and non-redundant, Algorithm1) is a measured self-evolution mechanism; the paper explicitly validates that Thought-Retriever improves as it answers more queries (Sec1), supporting MF's gotcha-consolidation premise.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (AcademicEval + public datasets, Sec4.2); TMLR-published (peer-reviewed, OpenReview link), a comparatively strong evidence base for this batch.

cita: Wu et al. (2026). GAM: Hierarchical Graph-based Agentic Memory for LLM Agents.
problema: Unified stream-based memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryOS, Mem0) update the active memory stream directly, causing Memory Loss (established nodes become disconnected/forgotten) and Semantic Drift (distinct topics erroneously conflated) from continuous noisy updates; discrete structured architectures (GraphRAG, LightRAG) are stable but too rigid to track an evolving narrative in real time.
mecanismo: Decouples encoding from consolidation via a state machine with two phases: an Episodic Buffering State appends incoming utterances to a local Event Progression Graph (fast, isolated, write-protected from the global store) until an LLM-driven semantic-divergence detector flags a topic boundary, triggering the Semantic Consolidation State, which merges the buffered subgraph into a dual-granularity node (summary + raw text) in the global Topic Associative Network via coarse-to-fine (vector top-5, then LLM-scored) edge linking; retrieval is a graph-guided top-down traversal (semantic anchoring + first-order expansion, then cross-layer drill-down into archived event graphs) re-ranked by a multiplicative semantic-probability x {temporal, confidence, role} boost.
evaluacion: LoCoMo (4 reasoning categories) and LongDialQA (multi-party TV-script dialogues) across 4 backbones (Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-7B/14B, GPT-4o-mini) vs 6 baselines (MemoryBank, ReadAgent, MemGPT, MemoryOS, Mem0, A-Mem); component ablation removing the Topic Associative Network, Event Progression Graph, state-switching mechanism, and multi-factor retrieval; a hyperparameter sensitivity sweep on the retrieval boosting factors.
numeros_clave: On Qwen2.5-7B, GAM surpasses Mem0 by over 18% in Temporal F1 on LoCoMo (Sec4.2); on GPT-4o-mini GAM's average F1 (43.14) is the best overall despite Mem0 leading specifically on Temporal F1 (56.42 vs 51.96); on LongDialQA with Qwen2.5-7B, GAM's average F1 12.55 surpasses MemoryOS by 86%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit Episodic-Buffering-vs-Semantic-Consolidation state machine, triggered only at LLM-detected semantic boundaries rather than fixed token/time steps (Sec3.3), is a concrete, measured (ablation-validated) trigger design for MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion timing.

The paper explicitly measures and names 'Memory Loss' and 'Semantic Drift' as failure modes of direct-write memory streams and shows GAM's write-isolation reduces them (Fig.1, Sec1), external evidence supporting MF's caution against uncontrolled single-stream memory writes.

Cross-layer edges (Ecross) explicitly bridge the separate global Topic graph and local/archived Event graphs (Sec3.2) -- a concrete multi-store seam pattern relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact debate, implemented as an index rather than deduplication.

notes: Numbers from Sec4.2 (LoCoMo/LongDialQA main results) plus the ablation study referenced in Sec4.3; solid multi-backbone, multi-dataset evaluation with an honest exception noted (Mem0 beats GAM on GPT-4o-mini Temporal F1).

cita: Li et al. (2026). CodeTracer: Towards Traceable Agent States.
problema: Coding agents orchestrate long, heterogeneous action sequences (search/read/edit/build/test) whose state transitions and error propagation are opaque; an early misstep can cascade into a hidden error chain, and existing tracing is limited to coarse pass/fail labels or small-scale manual inspection, which does not scale to diagnosing where and why a real trajectory went wrong.
mecanismo: A three-stage pipeline: (1) evolving extraction parses heterogeneous run-directory artifacts via a registry of reusable, adaptively-synthesized parsers into normalized typed step records; (2) tree indexing converts the flat step sequence into a hierarchical trace tree, collapsing pure-exploration steps under the current state node and only branching to a new state node on codebase/environment-changing actions; (3) diagnosis traverses the tree to localize the failure-responsible stage, error-relevant steps, and a compact evidence set, which can then be replayed back into the agent as a diagnostic prefix hint (reflective replay).
evaluacion: CodeTraceBench: 4,354 standardized, step-level-annotated trajectories from 5 SWE benchmarks x 4 agent frameworks x 5 backbones (human-annotated with Cohen's kappa=0.73 inter-annotator agreement on error-critical steps); evaluated via macro step-level Precision/Recall/F1 for failure localization against Bare-LLM and Mini-CodeTracer baselines, plus a component ablation and a reflective-replay recovery experiment.
numeros_clave: CodeTracer improves overall localization F1 to 46.6/48.0/46.1 (Claude/GPT-5/DeepSeek) from a Bare-LLM baseline of 16.2/18.8/16.3 (Table3); component ablation shows tree indexing alone contributes +18.3 F1 points and evolving extraction a further +9.4 points over Mini-CodeTracer (Table4); reflective replay raises Pass@1 on originally-failed runs for every backbone (e.g. Claude 23.9%->29.3%, Fig.6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The hierarchical trace tree that collapses pure-exploration steps under a state node and only branches on state-changing actions (Sec3.1, Fig.4) is a concrete derived-index-over-execution-history pattern MF could adapt for compressing agent-session logs into a navigable structure.

Ablation (Table4) measures that structural indexing (tree indexing +18.3 F1, evolving extraction +9.4 F1) beats raw-log prompting at lower token cost per instance, confirming MF's premise that structuring, not brute context-dumping, is the cost/quality lever.

Failure-onset localization with a compact, traceable evidence set justifying the diagnosis (Sec3.1, step-level P/R/F1 against a human-annotated gold error-critical step) is a rigorous provenance/verification pattern relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor, even though the domain is code-agent debugging rather than agent memory per se.

notes: Numbers from Table3 (main localization results) and Table4 (ablation) plus Fig.6 (replay); RECONSIDERAR -- this is fundamentally an agent-tracing/debugging benchmark paper (traceable execution state for SWE agents), with only WRITE+CONSOLIDACION as memory operations; its 'persistent memory' is a hierarchical trace tree of past actions, not an agent long-term memory system in the sense of the rest of this corpus.
